title: Retry once and log commit and record count when go can't resolve
summary: In `athena go` (go_job in crates/athena-core/src/run.rs), when `records.resolve` finds no job, log the HEAD commit and the number of records read via `ui.line`, reload records at the current HEAD, and resolve once more. Goal: make the unreproduced race in review item m7 diagnosable and self-healing for the maintainer.

defaults_applied.how: New tests plus cargo test and clippy criteria.
A criterion checks the retry and the log happening, not that code exists.
The behavior criteria run with cargo test.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Only `athena go` is changed; other callers of resolve are untouched.
Record count means the number of record files in the loaded set (or jobs); the producer picks one and the log line labels it.
The retry reloads HEAD, since the race is plausibly a stale head or a half-written commit.
Logging goes through the existing Ui::line.
The tests use the existing test harness; the test mechanism for injecting a first-load miss is the producer's choice.

acceptance_criteria.text: go_job in crates/athena-core/src/run.rs, on a 'no job matches' failure, emits a line through ui containing the HEAD commit id and the record count read, then re-reads HEAD and records and resolves once more.
The retry happens exactly once: a second failure returns the original no-match error, and 'latest', ambiguous matches, and other errors are not retried.

A new test shows a job that is absent from the first load but present at the retry resolves and runs, and a job that is never present fails after one retry with the log line emitted once. Run `cargo test`.
`cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
A CHANGELOG.md entry notes the log and retry, citing m7 in docs/design/reviews/athena-v0-acceptance-1.md.

out_of_scope: Finding the root cause of the m7 race.
Changing resolve semantics for other commands.
